The chmod widening (`0600`→`0644`, `0700`→`0755`) makes these locally-scoped secrets (GlitchTip API token, Slack webhook URL) world-readable on the host filesystem rather than just owner-readable. The tradeoff is clearly documented and reasoned about in the docstrings (Grafana's fixed non-root uid 472 needs to traverse/read across a native Linux bind mount with no uid remap), and these are described as low-value, locally-scoped tokens — I don't think this alone should block, but it's worth the human owner being aware this is a deliberate security/functionality tradeoff, not an oversight.

`terraform/main.tf`'s new `docker-compose.yml` bind mount uses `var.repo_path`, continuing the existing repo-relative resolution pattern this file already uses for `config.docker.ini`. This is consistent with the already-tracked "Repo-less Portability" debt in CLAUDE.md (Phase 6, separate issues) rather than a new violation introduced by this PR — not a blocking finding here, just noting it's not new debt.

issues.title: [dkblinux98/nyxGPT] Feature: feat: Linux-native install path - systemd units with OS dispatch (#3508) (PR #3611)
findings: Native web install destroys the previous working build before validating the new one succeeds

`_NATIVE_API_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE`/`_NATIVE_WEB_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE` hardcode `SYS_PY="/usr/bin/python3"` for reading `config.ini` at service start. This exactly mirrors the existing macOS Homebrew formula wrapper (where `/usr/bin/python3` is Apple's guaranteed system Python), but on Linux that path isn't universally guaranteed the same way, and the docs list the prerequisite as "Python 3.11+ ... on PATH" rather than at that specific path. Low risk on the mainstream distros the docs target (Ubuntu/Debian/Fedora/Arch all ship it there), but a `command -v python3` fallback would be more robust.

`scripts/follow-ollama-logs.sh`'s Linux candidate (`$HOME/.nyxGPT/logs/ollama-native.log`) is checked last, after `${prefix:-}/var/log/ollama.log` (which becomes plain `/var/log/ollama.log` when `brew` isn't present). On a Linux host that happens to have an unrelated system-level `/var/log/ollama.log` (e.g. a distro-packaged Ollama service), the script would tail the wrong file instead of falling through to the nyxGPT-managed one. Narrow edge case, not blocking.

findings: `nyxgpt ops env-sync` silently drops `.env.example` defaults when run before `nyxgpt ops install`

`pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` entry (`"nyxgpt.resources" = ["**/*", ".env.example"]`) globs the `docker/`/`ops/`/`scripts/` symlinked directories without any exclusion list. `docker/config.docker.ini` (gitignored, written pre-#3621 directly into `REPO_ROOT/docker/`, containing `[auth] api_key`/`[monitoring] grafana_admin_password`/an error-tracking DSN — see `_generate_compose_config`, `ops.py:1543`) is not tracked in git so a clean checkout won't pick it up, but a dev machine that ran pre-#3621 `nyxgpt ops install` and still has that stale artifact sitting in its checkout would have it silently swept into any wheel built from that tree (e.g. via `nyxgpt ops package` or `test_resources_packaging.py`). Worth an explicit exclude for defense-in-depth given this PR is explicit groundwork for publishing installable artifacts (CLAUDE.md's "Repo-less Portability" requirement).

`test_sync_env_from_config_creates_env_from_example` (`tests/unit/test_ops.py:1412`) still has `monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "REPO_ROOT", tmp_path)`, which is now a no-op leftover from before this PR's `env_path.parent`-relative resolution — harmless but worth cleaning up since it no longer does anything.

The new `test_repo_root_allowlist.py` guard matches on exact stripped source lines, so any unrelated `black` reformat of an allowlisted line will fail the test until the allowlist string is updated too — intentional per the docstring, but worth being aware of as a source of "unrelated" CI friction going forward.
